h: Shabbos Joins Human Guarding With the Gift of Divine Holiness

p: to say that they are equal
That is, the sum of the words of Torah
is "I am" and "You shall not have,"
which we heard from the mouth of the Almighty.
which are to eradicate the evil
from "the heart of the fool at his left" (Koheles 10:2),
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת קה, ב)
in the manner of what is stated (Shabbos 105b):
that is in a person's body?
Say, this is the yetzer hara."
And "I am" includes the positive mitzvos,
that holiness should shine in the heart
from the utterance "I am Hashem your God."
And this is "If you walk in My statutes"
it includes all the positive mitzvos,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים קיט, א)
in the manner of what is said (Tehillim 119:1):
"Fortunate are those whose way is perfect,
who walk in the Torah of Hashem."
but that of a mitzvah exempts you";
for one occupied with a mitzvah
is called the "walking" of the Merciful One.
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סוֹטָה ה, א)
in the manner of what is stated (Sotah 5a):
it is nothing but a prohibition."
And Shabbos is the sum of the positive mitzvos:
to bring the holiness of Shabbos
into "the heart of the wise man at his right";
"to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you";
and this is the sum of the positive mitzvos:
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים)
(as stated in Midrash Tanchuma, beginning of Parshas Kedoshim).
were said in a single utterance
for the main thing is "remember" with the mouth,
to receive the holiness of Shabbos,
so that they not hold one back
from receiving the holiness of Shabbos.
Torah study was implanted in their hearts,
and with the utterance "You shall not have"
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת יִשָּׁקֵנִי)
(as stated in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2, "Let him kiss me").
and in which forgetting does not exist
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב צב, ב)
for even though the yetzer hara returned to its place
"You speak with us and we will hear"
(as stated in Shir HaShirim Rabbah there),
nevertheless with the receiving of the Tablets,
it would have been "engraved on the Tablets"
that the yetzer hara not enter
so that the Shabbos would not be kept,
and one could not receive the holiness.
"And you shall remember that you were a slave
in the land of Egypt, etc.;
therefore Hashem your God commanded you
So too in the passage "And they shall keep"
and nothing was needed from man's side
is to receive the holiness from Hashem Yisbarach,
and for this the Exodus from Egypt is mentioned,
שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
which was also from Hashem Yisbarach's side,
only guarding is needed from man's side,
that they not desecrate it, Heaven forbid,
to receiving the holiness of Shabbos.
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב
and this too is according to what is written
"Shin is the secret of the three Avos,
and the 'daughter' is crowned with them"
'The fear of Hashem is His treasure';
I will fill your treasuries, etc."
And this is as the explanation written
and Shabbos is its name, etc."
"The Holy One, blessed be He, has
only a treasury of the fear of Heaven."
And this is what is said (Mishlei 8:21):
"To bestow substance upon those who love Me,
and their treasuries I will fill"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א ה, א)
And this is what it says:
And above, at the end of Behar,
with "If you walk in My statutes,"
in order to juxtapose "in My statutes"
which is to receive the holiness,
Also, here it speaks of a condition:
at the receiving of the Torah:
"I am," and afterward "You shall not have"
and afterward, as a matter of course,
as it was before the corruption:
הָאֱלֹקִים עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כט)
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ)
And this is what they said (Midrash Rabbah, beginning of this parshah, Vayikra Rabbah 35:1):
וְאַשְׁרֵי דְּרָכַי יִשְׁמוֹרוּ כּוּלֵּי (מִשְׁלֵי ח, לב)
and fortunate are those who keep my ways,' etc. (Mishlei 8:32):
fortunate am I and fortunate are you
that the will of the Omnipresent is
"I am," and afterward "You shall not have."
which is the "walking" of the Merciful One,
that the yetzer hara be uprooted.

paragraphs.text: Source: Vayikra Rabbah 35:2 — “דבר אחר, אם בחקתי תלכו, הדא הוא דכתיב (משלי ח, לב): ועתה בנים שמעו לי ואשרי דרכי ישמרו, מדבר ביעקב דכתיב ביה (בראשית כח, כ): וידר יעקב נדר לאמר, רבנן …” — “Another matter, “if you follow My statutes” – that is what is written: “Now, sons, heed me, as happy are those who observe my ways” (Proverbs 8:32). This is speaking of Jacob, in whose regard it is written: “Jacob took …”
